integrity: The two-dimensional result is an analytic minimization over every positive diagonal similarity. The three-dimensional obstruction is an exact parametric family with explicit spectrum, left and right eigenvectors, condition numbers, balancing similarity, and Frobenius-norm change. Historical harmful-balancing results are treated as prior work; the claim is restricted to simultaneous 2x2 optimality, minimal dimension three, and the explicit family.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns exact Osborne 2-norm balancing of irreducible real matrices and absolute conditioning of simple eigenvalues. It does not classify power-of-two approximations, finite-precision stopping rules, eigenvector conditioning, backward error, or the globally largest possible harmful factor in dimension three.
title: Exact 2-norm balancing is eigenvalue-condition optimal in dimension two, but dimension three is already harmful
